arg1.description: dtype-like object. In typical usage, this will be a dtype specifier, such as ``"float32"`` (i.e. a string), ``np.dtype('int32')`` (i.e. an instance of :class:`numpy.dtype`), ``jnp.complex64`` (i.e. a JAX scalar constructor), or ``np.uint8`` (i.e. a NumPy scalar type).
constraints: arg1 must be JAX/NumPy compatible dtype
arg1 and arg2 must be JAX/NumPy compatible dtypes

arg2.description: dtype-like object. In typical usage, this will be a generic scalar type, such as ``jnp.integer``, ``jnp.floating``, or ``jnp.complexfloating``.
constraints: arg2 must be JAX/NumPy compatible dtype
arg1 and arg2 must be JAX/NumPy compatible dtypes

output.description: True if arg1 represents a dtype that is equal or lower in the type hierarchy than arg2.

constraints: arg1 and arg2 must be JAX/NumPy compatible dtypes
